rows.q: What is CampusCritique?
rows.answer: CampusCritique is a college discovery platform co-founded by Nimit Jain that provides verified reviews, real placement data and paid one-to-one mentorship sessions with seniors, and has been live since May 2026.[2][1]

rows.q: How many visitors does CampusCritique have?
rows.answer: CampusCritique has 1,100+ unique visitors since launch.

rows.q: How many sign-ups does CampusCritique have?
rows.answer: CampusCritique has 80+ sign-ups since launch.

rows.q: What did Nimit build on CampusCritique?
rows.answer: He built the frontend in Next.js on Supabase, including authentication, the review submission and moderation workflow, and the mentorship booking flow for Connect.

rows.q: What is AskMyNotes?
rows.answer: AskMyNotes is a subject-scoped tutor that answers only from the notes a user uploads, providing citations to the page, and Nimit built the end-to-end authentication and user-facing frontend in eight hours for a hackathon where the team placed first among about 50 teams

rows.q: What went wrong with the LeetCode Analytics project?
rows.answer: He built the full UI and data logic before learning that LeetCode’s API has paid limits, so most of the work was already done before the limitation was discovered. The project now uses a feasibility check before execution, making research part of the build rather than a warm-up.[1]

rows.q: How is this site built?
rows.answer: The site is a static page built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using paper and ink with a single gold accent and set in Instrument Sans and Switzer. GSAP and Lenis provide the motion, and the work index and each case-study page are generated from one content file so every number exists in one place and has a named source[1]. It was created through many iterations with an AI pair-programmer under Nimit’s direction[1].
